basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 3.' and it opens '(Vers. 3.) Vixit autem Adam ducentos et triginta annos, et genuit ad imaginem et'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 3.) Vixit autem Adam ducentos et triginta annos, et genuit ad imaginem et similitudinem suam, et vocavit nomen ejus Seth. Sciendum quod usque ad diluvium, ubi in nostris codicibus, ducentorum et quod excurrit annorum genuisse quis dicitur: in Hebraeo habeat centum annos, et reliquos qui sequuntur.
